reason: Both are unusable thin-banner resizes, with the photo reduced to a tiny thumbnail and a huge empty field. A: the photo is a tiny thumbnail, the white heart is a near-invisible faint outline with stray edge marks, the text is tiny and stacked in the centre with the URL jammed underneath, and the rest is dead space. B: the heart is a ghost outline cut into the page with no content, the photo is tiny, and the URL is stranded at the far right, away from the headline. B's headline is larger and more readable, and the layout is cleaner and more balanced than A's, but it is still broken.

Both lose the hero barrel photo, shrinking it to a tiny thumbnail at the bottom, so the design no longer resembles the original. A also has a heavy black smeared bar in the middle that looks like a rendering glitch, and the logo is a tiny icon. The watercolor wash floats as a detached rectangle with hard edges. B has no black bar, but its em-dash is stranded at the top, the elements are scattered with no grouping, and the logo and thumbnail are tiny. B is slightly less broken than A, mainly because of A's black bar.

A: The headline is large and the doctor art is intact. But the symptom list butts right up against 'SYMPTOMS' with almost no gutter, and it is cramped against the top edge. The hashtag bar is stretched wide and its text is tiny. The CTA is small and the whole layout is crowded, though nothing overlaps. B: There is a clean headline and a more orderly stack, but the doctor is cropped into a small chunk with a hard edge at the bottom-right. The hashtag bar is a wide strip with tiny text. The CTA is tiny and low in the layout next to an oversized sparkle that has lost its meaning. The list reads 'Dry cough Sore throat Headache' as run-on lines, and there is big dead space at the top and left.

A: the hashtag is crushed into a tiny yellow bar and the call-to-action text is microscopic and unreadable, and the headline is small. There is dead space on the left and between the text and the doctor, and the list items are ragged. B: the headline is large and the hashtag banner is legible, so the hierarchy holds. The flaws are a cramped list that wraps awkwardly ("Shortness of / breath Dry / cough"), the headline nearly touching the list, and the CTA squeezed against the doctor's feet.

A keeps the white label panel, headline order and illustrations, so it reads as the same design. Flaws: two stray divider lines float outside the panel at the right, a small dash sits on the left bottle, soap-like fragments are cropped at the bottom, and the panel crowds the top. B is broken: the white panel is empty and displaced to the right, text sits unframed on the beige, the order is wrong (J'adore Paris below the headline), illustrations are shrunk to a tiny strip, and divider lines are orphaned.

A keeps the brand text readable and stacks it in a sensible top-to-bottom flow, and the illustrations are reasonably sized and scattered down the tall strip. Flaws: an empty white label frame floats in the middle as dead space, the headline order is jumbled (LAVANDER, HOMEMADE LOTION, J'adore Paris), and the illustrations are fragmented. B is worse. Its illustrations shrink to a tiny strip, the white frame holds only stray divider lines, 'HOMEMADE LOTION' is misaligned and orphaned below the frame, and large dead areas fill the rest, so the design is unrecognisable.

A shrinks the owl mascots to tiny, almost invisible icons in the bottom-left corner, so the brand imagery is lost. The text is jammed at the top with a large dead confetti area below, and the red subtitle competes with the headline. B keeps the owls at a meaningful size beside a large, clear three-line headline, so it reads as the same design. Its flaws: 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' is tiny and stranded at the top-left, far from the headline; the top half is mostly empty confetti; and the owl pair is slightly cramped next to the title.

A: the headline is tiny and jammed against the top edge, and the owls are shrunk to illegible specks under the text. The confetti sits far off to the right as dead scatter, and the left third is empty. The subtitle reads as bigger than it should, and the whole thing looks like a shrunk copy. B: reads left to right, the headline is large and dominant, and the owls are recognisable beside it. Flaws: the owls touch or crowd the headline, and the order is flipped so "Event Management" sits far left and detached. The confetti is a faint scatter in the middle gap, and the right edge margin is tight. Still the better layout, but not shippable.

A: the quote has an orphaned 'INDEED,' line and is crammed at the top with the attribution jammed right under it. The image strip floats mid-page, and the bottom third is a large dead white area, so the layout is unbalanced. B: the headline is large and clear, and the image is trimmed at the top with the text below it, which is a sensible order. Flaws: 'INDEED,' sits alone on its own line, the headline has very loose leading, the attribution lines are tightly stacked, and the image strip is small. Overall B uses the space better and has the stronger hierarchy.

A is broken: the SALE letters are scattered and detached from their circles, with E stranded far above 'S A L'. The circles are crushed into a tiny cluster at the bottom-left. The headline is crossed by the stray letters and is not the focal point. Large dead areas remain, and the decor is shrunk to tiny. B keeps the headline readable at the top and the SALE circles with the lantern tassel as a unit. Its flaws: letters are misplaced (S, A L, blank, E), so the word is unreadable. The circles are cramped at the right edge, and the decor is duplicated and small.

A uses the tall canvas, but the headline is small and the characters are scattered with large dead areas. MERRY and DISCOUNT are separated by a big gap, and the bottom row of characters looks sparse and disconnected. B keeps the original composition shrunk into a thin horizontal band, with huge empty areas above and below and tiny text. That is the classic shrink-not-rearrange failure, though the cluster is cohesive and the headline and subline sit close together. Both are weak; A at least rearranges and fills the format more.

A breaks the lockup: the headline is small and floats at the top while the gold leaf wreath is separated from it, sits as an empty arc over the dark cloth and overlaps the fig. The text no longer reads as the focal point and the brand mark is lost. B keeps the wreath wrapped around a large 'Perfect Taste', so it stays the same design. It is slightly crowded by the fig at the bottom of the wreath and the wreath is a little off-centre, but those are minor polish items.

A: the quote is tiny with a big dead gap from the illustration, and the attribution 'CAROLYN MURPHY' is larger than the quote lines, so the hierarchy is inverted. The illustration is a small thumbnail with a placeholder 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION' label, and the left edge is cramped. B: the quote is large and clearly the headline, and the illustration is a bit bigger and fairly well framed. Flaws: the attribution floats detached on the far right and small, the same placeholder text is inside the frame, and the quote is not tied to the frame as in the original.

A keeps the white frame with corner nodes and the brand orange tint, so it reads as the same design. But the frame is empty, the reading order is jumbled (tickets text sits above the 'Theatre presents' line), the copy is cramped with uneven sizes, and the oversized play icon in the bottom bar is cropped at the left edge. B loses the white frame and turns the orange panel into a blank block over a dark, purple-shifted image, so the brand colour and feel are damaged. B has the same jumbled text order, a faint box artifact next to the icon, and a play icon jammed into the corner.

A: very wide banner with tiny, illegible body, legal and URL text. The subhead is microscopic and cramped under the headline. The URL is jammed beside the CTA. A large empty right column holds only tiny text, so the hierarchy is broken and the layout is unbalanced. B: logo is shrunk but intact, and the headline is large and clear with a readable left-to-right flow. The subhead wraps awkwardly, with orphans like 'virtual' and 'challenges?'. The CTA is stacked into a narrow 5-line column that is hard to read. The right-hand text is tiny and the layout is crowded and edge-tight, so it is still flawed, but clearly better than A.

Both are unusable on a 160x600 canvas with a white background. A: the headline is clipped at the top of the image band ("Special" is cut off), and "March 21" is nearly invisible cream on white. The CTA, tagline and body copy are all missing. B: the headline is fully legible and sits wholly inside the dark panel, but "Joint celebration" is cut off at the panel edge. "March 21" is cream on white and unreadable, the divider lines float on white, and the body copy and URL are missing. B loses less and keeps the headline intact, so it is less bad.

A: headline is larger and more dominant, with a clean left-text/right-art split and the cats anchored to the bottom edge like the original. Flaws: the illustration is small and jammed into the far right corner, and there is a large empty gap between the text and the art. B: the cats sit more centrally and are slightly larger, but the headline is noticeably smaller and weaker. The cat group floats with its feet clipped at the bottom edge, and the text is pushed right of centre, so the overall balance is less deliberate.

A: the headline 'Order online' is shrunk and pushed to the bottom, below 'food & drinks', so the reading order is reversed. The rules no longer frame the copy and there is a big gap in the middle, but all text stays on the clean background and is legible. B: the headline is tiny and floats between the rules, 'food & drinks' is detached and overlaps the box photo, and the rules frame nothing. The hierarchy is inverted and the layout looks arbitrary.

A keeps the big tan/red '04' block recognisable and puts the headline on a clean white panel; flaws: the 'ART' top row is cropped and jumbled, and a hairline/striped artifact sits at the panel edge near the top. The art is cut and crowded on the right, and the headline is small with a lot of empty white. B crops the hero tan/red numerals into unrecognisable fragments, so the original look is lost. Its white panel is oversized and ragged, with the headline off-centre inside it, and the fragmented letters at the bottom edge look messy.

A: the text sits on a white box pasted over the art, cramped to the left, with a big pink/magenta ART dominating the right and pulling focus from the headline. The art is chopped and jumbled, the original composition is lost, and the text is small. B: the text is on a clean white area on the right, with the tan/red art keeping the original look and reading order. Flaws: the right side has clipped T fragments, the top ART row is cut off, and the text is small with uneven margins.

A rearranges the design: large three-line headline with the blue/black colour split intact, and two aligned boxes below as a clear group. Flaws: the headline sits on the busy image, its end clips the pillar, and a decorative ball is cut at the left edge. The boxes are small with dead space beneath them, and the boxes sit on the busy photo. B is a stretched copy of the banner: the headline is small and runs flush to the left edge with its 'C' cropped, so it is not a rearrangement. The blue and black boxes are staggered and misaligned, the black box touches the right edge, and the bottom half of the canvas is dead space. Body text in B is also small.

A scrambles the reading order: "Xavier Sport Program" sits above "by submitting to", so the sentence reads backwards. The blue box is jammed against the top edge, it covers the racket and the top of the ball, and the text sizes are inconsistent and cramped. The dividers and the thin frame are lost. B keeps the correct order (Win a study grant / by submitting to / Xavier Sport Program) in a clean blue panel with the ball and racket visible above it. Its flaws are tiny, hard-to-read secondary text, "Program" orphaned on its own line, a two-column split inside the panel that feels odd, and a panel that crowds the ball and sits low against the bottom edge. It is still the more coherent and brand-faithful layout.

A keeps the original's blue card, text hierarchy and thin frame intact, but the card overlaps the ball and racket awkwardly, the frame line cuts through the racket and card at an arbitrary position, the image looks soft/upscaled, and the text is small in the large canvas. B breaks the lockup: 'by submitting to' is split into a tiny, ragged three-line fragment beside 'Xavier Sport Program', the rule lines are orphaned and run into the edges, the ball is cropped to a sliver, and the huge panel feels heavy; it loses the original's centred, intentional structure.

A keeps the original's order and pairing: Rough with PRAY on the left, then the divider, then Great with PRAY, then the rose. Flaws: the pairs are misaligned, so Rough sits high and PRAY floats low, the divider is heavy and oddly placed, the rose is small and cropped square, and nothing stands out as headline or CTA. B is jumbled. PRAY, Great, Rough and PRAY are stacked in a ragged staircase with different sizes and mismatched alignments. The divider is stranded at far left, away from the text. The Rough/Great pairing and the reading order are lost, so the arrangement has no apparent intent.

A: tiny 'Sets for kids $14.99' text is illegible, the brick is a tiny fragment, 'Buy 2 only for' collides with the ORDER NOW button, the price is lost and the left side has a big empty gap. B: the headline is large and readable, though broken as 'CONS TRUC TION'. The brick graphic is cramped and overlapped by 'Buy 2 only for', the price is small and detached after the button, and the CTA is small and sits before the price. It is cluttered but all content is present and mostly legible.

A: headline is clean and left-anchored, but 'CONS TRUC TION' is split into three words with awkward spacing. The brick is tiny and cropped by the X shape in the top right. The price is detached from 'Buy 2 only for' and sits after the CTA, so the reading order is jumbled. There is a large dead area on the left and the right side is scattered. B: the X graphic is huge but the brick is a tiny cropped fragment, so the key product image is lost. Headline has the same 'CONS TRUC TION' break. The price is separated from 'Buy 2 only for', which sits far right beside the CTA. The CTA text is tiny, and the cluster feels disjointed. B's price and brick grouping is better than A's price placement, but the lost product hurts it more.

A keeps the purple circle as a backing panel with 'Smart Home' above 'GADGETS' in the right order and readable white text. Flaws: the text is small, the text block sits low-left inside the shape, the dots are cramped, and the frame line is faint. B has the order reversed ('GADGETS' above 'Smart Home'), and the text sits directly on the busy wood and robot image with no panel behind it. The purple shape is shrunk to a tiny fragment at the bottom, the dots and frame are leftovers, and the brand shape is lost, so it is barely usable.

Both are unusable: all text (headline, URL, logo wordmark) is missing, leaving an empty blue block and tiny photo. A has the logo icon in outline stuck at lower right next to a tiny photo, with large dead areas and a blank grey strip. B has the logo at the top, a stray diagonal line artifact running through the stack, a larger blank grey box, and the photo is tiny. B's vertical flow (logo, banner, photo) is slightly more ordered, but both fail.

A: the photo is a small thumbnail at far left, the white heart shape floats empty and detached from the text, and the URL is stranded far to the right, so there's large dead space and no CTA. Text is a readable size and the group is vertically centred. B: the photo is smaller and the text is tiny. The heart is a near-invisible white outline, and the URL is jammed under the headline. The layout is compressed into the middle of the banner, with huge empty margins. A is slightly better because its text is bigger and more legible.

A: text is mostly legible and the hashtag, headline, list and doctor are all present. But the list is cramped against the headline, the 'Dry cough' wrap is awkward, and the CTA is jammed against the doctor's illustration. The yellow hashtag bar is stretched wide with tiny text, and the left side is crowded. B: a calmer, more intentional composition, but the hashtag text in the yellow bar and the CTA are microscopic and unreadable. Symptoms list text is tiny, the headline dominates, and the sparkle is orphaned beside the CTA. Large dead space surrounds the content. Readability failure outweighs the cleaner look.

A is broken: the white label panel is empty and stranded at right, stray rules float in space, the order is jumbled (Lavander, then Homemade Lotion, then J'adore Paris), and the illustrations are shrunk into a tiny strip. B keeps the label frame, the correct order and large illustrations. Its flaws are two stray rules sticking out of the panel's right edge, a small line fragment over the left bottle, and uneven illustration spacing with a cropped biscuit.

A: the original's brand frame is lost and replaced by an orphan flat orange rectangle over the image; the orange tint is gone (dark purple look). The text stack is jumbled, with tickets before 'presents' and 'Music and lyrics' last. The forward icon is jammed in the bottom corner with a stray box. B: keeps the original's orange tint, the white frame with its dots and dividers, and the same palette, so it reads as the same design. It has the same bad text order (tickets above 'Richmond High School Theatre presents') and tight, uneven line sizes. The frame is empty and decorative, and the dark footer band with the icon is awkward, but it's more coherent.

Both are unusable. A keeps the full headline inside the dark forest block, but "Joint celebration" is clipped at the block edge. The "March 21" date is cream on white and invisible, the divider lines are invisible, and the supporting copy and URL are missing. B clips the first line of the headline ("Special" is cut off at the top), runs the headline over the pale sky band so contrast is poor, and puts the date on white where it is nearly invisible. B also drops the subhead, body and URL, and is mostly empty white. A is slightly less bad because its headline is complete and readable.

A scrambles reading order: 'PRAY' sits above 'When Life Is Great' and the 'Rough' pair is split with a small 'PRAY' below. Text is ragged and unaligned, the divider is stranded at the far left, and the rose is cut off at the edge. B keeps each phrase paired with its PRAY and reads left to right: Rough/PRAY, divider, Great/PRAY, rose. Its flaws are the left pair being larger and offset from the right pair, uneven sizes, a thick divider that departs from the original's hairline, and a lot of empty space.

A is broken: the headline is split, with 'GET A GIFT' tiny at left and 'with your next cup of coffee' in huge white text over the busy sweater and mug, so it is hard to read and collides with the image. The 'Only this Christmas' and URL text is microscopic, the stars are oversized, the dashed lines cross the photo, and the reading order is jumbled. B keeps the copy in one centred block on clean pink, with the order intact and no collisions with the photo. Its flaws are tiny type (URL, 'Only this Christmas', logo), a large dead pink area to the left of the block, a cramped icon row, and a headline that is too small for the banner.

A keeps the photo, headline and URL grouped in one centered column with a sensible reading order (image, headline, URL). Its flaws are that the white heart/X shape is faint and cropped at the bottom-left, which looks like a stray artifact, and the layout is a narrow strip with big dead gaps and a tiny photo. B puts the large empty outlined heart shape in the middle of the canvas, separating the photo from the text. The shape reads as a blank placeholder and the headline is detached from the image. B has the same small photo and dead space, and its grouping and balance are worse.

A keeps the original composition intact (white card, frame, dots, correct reading order) but it is only a letterboxed shrink. White bands top and bottom waste space, and the card text is the same small size, so it fits the square format poorly. B is broken: a pink dot collides with the 'STUDIO' text, 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' sits below the headline, and the order is jumbled. The frame is a stray empty rectangle, the dot floats in it, and the tagline bar sticks out of the card edge. The opening line is cramped to the card edges and the card is oddly narrow and offset.

A keeps the original's overlap, but the white text straddles the red/blue edge of the T stem ("AGAINST CRUELTY" and "TO ANIMALS" cross or touch it), so it looks accidental. "NOW!" is orphaned on its own line, and the cluster floats centred with dead blue on both sides. B has no collisions and consistent contrast, with a clean left-to-right text block and the T at the right with a margin. It loses the layering, has no size hierarchy in the copy, the text is small for the canvas, and the left side is empty.

A reads left to right as a banner: headline, tagline, teal callout, and booking info are in a sensible order with good contrast. Flaws: the booking text is tiny and nearly illegible, the dashes are scattered fragments, and the callout wraps into three lines. B is a jammed cluster in the right half with a large dead area on the left. The headline is small and crammed at the top edge, and the lines are cramped and nearly touching. The tagline is centred against left-aligned lines, the dashed line is stranded at the bottom, and the booking text is microscopic. That makes it unusable.

Both are broken and unusable. A keeps the headline, brand name and URL together in a readable block, but the photos are tiny, the empty frames and stray ornaments are scattered, and a large pattern tile is left. The 'RESTAURANT' text is also misordered. B has a bigger headline, but the photos are minuscule inside empty panels and the logo text is orphaned at the bottom. Its ornaments are scattered and the layout is a fragmented mess with no clear product imagery.

A keeps the correct reading order, with 'WE CREATE' above 'MARKETING FUTURE' on the left. The headline is readable and the 'Join WADE team' block is stacked on the right. Flaws: the decorative X/O/lines float in a large dead centre, the CTA is tiny and crammed against the right edge over a dark photo patch, and the maroon panel is reduced to slivers. B scrambles the order: 'WE CREATE' sits below the headline, 'team WADE' is tiny and wedged into the shapes, and the giant 'Join' on the far right is cut off by the edge and separated from 'team WADE'. A stray maroon box and a line run through a hand. The message is jumbled and the hierarchy is wrong.

A: the headline is large and clear, the image sits at the top like the original, and the attribution is subordinate in coral. Flaws: the crowd image is shrunk to a thin strip, the quote breaks into 8 short lines, and the attribution lines are tightly leaded and close to the bottom edge. B: the image floats in the middle with dead space above and below, and the text is tiny. The quote wraps raggedly ('OF THOUGHTFUL' on its own line, an uneven rag), the attribution is cramped, and the whole composition is lost in whitespace with no hierarchy.

A: headline is large, readable and centered on one axis, but the logo and shapes are shrunk to a tiny cropped strip under the text, so the brand mark is nearly lost and the deco shapes look clipped. B: the logo and shapes are also tiny and clipped, floating at the far left, and the headline is a 4-line stack that crowds the canvas height with large dead space on both sides. The logo and headline are disconnected, and the layout is lopsided. A's headline reads cleaner as 2 lines and hierarchy is clearer, so it is less bad.

A keeps the SALE lantern column intact and the decor fills the canvas. But the S/A/L/E letters sit at the bottom of their circles instead of centred, and the circles are mostly empty. The headline is small and orphaned at top-left, with a tiny decor cluster at top-right and a big dead gap, so the hierarchy and balance are weak. B breaks the design: the SALE letters are scattered as tiny, out-of-order characters (E, then S, A, L) with the headline wedged between them, and the circles and tassel are gone. A small decor cluster floats in the middle, and the bottom half is empty with a stray tiny fragment, so the message is lost.

A scrambles the SALE sequence (E sits above the headline, then S-A-L), the circular badges are lost, the letters are loose and tiny, and there is a large dead gap plus a cramped, unreadable cluster at the bottom, so it is unusable. B keeps the headline on top and rebuilds the four SALE circles in a column with the tassel, which is recognisably the original. But the letter sizes vary (S and E large, A and L small), the lantern art is duplicated and tiny, and there is dead space in the middle.

Both are 320x50 banners that read DISCOUNT before MERRY, which reverses the original order. A: the MERRY wordmark is at least legible and sits close to the DISCOUNT block, but the right side is a cramped cluster of tiny characters pushed against the edge. DISCOUNT dominates, and there is no clear CTA. B: DISCOUNT is large, but the MERRY wordmark is shrunk to near-illegible size and sits low in a scattered row of tiny props. The characters are stranded at the far edges, so the brand wordmark is lost and the layout looks fragmented.

A is broken: a flat orange placeholder block sits in the banner, "Pygmalion" is tiny at the top, and the CTA and presenter line are crammed together. The "RICHMOND HIGH SCHOOL THEATRE PRESENTS" text collides with the arrow icon, and the sizes barely step so there is no hierarchy. B reads left to right: presenter line, large headline, subtitle, then the CTA with the arrow icon. Its flaws are a tiny, narrow-wrapped presenter text at far left, a stray orange bar that looks like a leftover block, and an oversized arrow icon competing with the headline.

A keeps the diamond mosaic and both brown badges, and the headline, rule and body copy stay grouped as in the original. Its flaws are a hard flat crop on the photo band, large dead white bands above and below, and small body and vertical URL text. B breaks the mosaic: the diamond layout is distorted with empty white holes, stray ghost slivers sit at the bottom edge, and the address badge floats loose. The rule also detaches from the headline and sits on the body copy, leaving a big gap under the headline. B is clearly less faithful and less intentional.

A: logo, headline and body keep a clear hierarchy, and the URL is promoted to a legible, larger line. Flaws: the legal/event-details text is tiny and pushed far from the URL at the bottom, which breaks the original reading order (details before link). It also leaves a dead gap in the lower third. B: the URL and the event-details copy are both very small and nearly illegible at 300x600. The CTA link is buried and the whole text block is cramped. The tiny type is the key failure, though the grouping and order are intact.

A keeps the original's reading order (price, subline, vertical URL, product list) and the three colour stripes as a header motif; flaws are the stripes being tiny and detached, the white card lost, very small text, and dead space at the bottom. B is scrambled: the URL sits top-left away from the price, the 'for all drinkware on' line is a tiny fragment beside a grey block, the price comes after it, and the stripes are cropped into the bottom corner. It has a broken hierarchy, an arbitrary grey rectangle and unreadably small copy.

A reads left to right as a banner: large headline left and the cat group right, both clearly legible. Flaws: the line break puts 'AND' alone on a middle line, the text block sits close to the left edge, the art nearly touches the bottom, and the right side has tight margins. B stacks everything vertically, which suits a banner badly. Its headline is small, and the art is a small cluster in the centre with big dead purple areas on both sides. The headline is jammed against the top edge and detached from the art. The hierarchy is weak, and it looks like a shrunk copy of the poster.

Both scatter the three text elements far apart and lose the original's rule–headline–subline lockup, leaving large dead areas. A is worse: the 'Order online' headline is tiny (about 12px) and smaller than 'food & drinks', so hierarchy is inverted and the message is nearly unreadable. B has a larger headline that is bolder than the subline, but it is still small for the canvas. B also reads in the wrong order, with 'food & drinks' above 'Order online', and the headline is detached from the subline and jammed near the bottom rule.

A: headline runs nearly edge to edge and is small, the dark box sits directly under it and is tiny with small text, the blue box order is swapped against the original, and there is a big empty gap in the middle. B: headline is larger and stacked to 4 lines with a clear hierarchy, and both boxes are grouped at the bottom with readable text. Flaws in B: the 'Festival' orphan line, the blue box text is small, the headline sits close to the left edge, and a dead image area sits in the middle.

A: the blue panel is a coherent block and all copy reads in order (headline, 'by submitting to', brand). But the panel is bottom-heavy with a large empty blue area below the text, a stray thin outline box floats over the racket, there are odd underline fragments under 'submitting' and 'Program', the panel edge has a notch, and 'by submitting to' sits beside the brand instead of above it. B: reading order is wrong, because 'Xavier Sport Program' comes before 'by submitting to'. The headline is left-ragged and off-center inside the panel, the text is cramped against the left edge with a large empty bottom area, and a stray blue rectangle is cut off at the top edge. Orphaned line fragments sit at the bottom. It looks broken and unintentional.

A: headline reads in the wrong order ("FAMILY DAYS OUT IN" top-left, "London" right, so the break reads oddly). The grey panel is orphaned mid-canvas and a stray rectangle sits at the bottom. Chevrons are a loose row over busy imagery, and the subline is small, over a busy skyline. B: the subline "Save your money, enjoy your weekend" is dark text over the dense city and is nearly illegible. The headline order is reversed ("London" above "FAMILY DAYS OUT IN"). The chevrons are cut off at the bottom edge and a stray grey bar floats at the top. B is worse because key copy is unreadable and cropped.

Both candidates clip the purple circle with a hard vertical edge at the right, leaving a stray wood strip. The thin frame bisects the circle and the wood in an arbitrary way. A's headline is slightly smaller, and its dot pattern is pushed to the far right edge, away from the frame and text. B's 'GADGETS' is a little larger and its dot column sits closer to the composition, but its dots also touch the circle edge and the frame. The two are nearly equivalent, with B marginally better.

A is missing the headline, URL and logo wordmark entirely. The logo icon is detached and sits grey and faint on white, outside the banner. B keeps the headline, URL and logo inside the blue band, readable and on brand. B still has large dead white space above and below the banner, so the design is a tiny strip on a square canvas. The logo and text are also small.

A scatters the pieces across the tall canvas. The BEDDING wordmark is small and sits left, detached from the logo. The "& Baby Toddler" logo is tiny and floats off-axis, the image strip hovers in a different place, and the dot patterns are nearly invisible. There is no grouping or hierarchy and most of the canvas is dead space, so it is unusable. B keeps the original banner lockup (image, logo, BEDDING, dots) intact and in the right reading order, so it stays recognisably the same design. But it is just the banner shrunk into a thin strip in the middle of a tall canvas. Huge empty areas sit above and below, the text is small, the dots touch the canvas edges, and the logo crowds the image. It is still the clearly better of the two, but it is not shippable.

Both are broken: the illustrations are shrunk to tiny strips and split into two disconnected halves, and the artwork is lost. A: the wordmark is full width but it has a huge dead gap between the illustrations and the tagline, and the tagline floats near the bottom with no grouping. B: the headline and tagline sit together as a unit, and the tagline is bigger, but the art is tiny and pushed to the top edge, and the text nearly touches the side margins. B's grouping is slightly better than A's scattered layout.

Both are tiny 320x50 banners with the MERRY logo shrunk to a tiny size. A puts DISCOUNT in the middle with MERRY squeezed below it, which breaks the original reading order (MERRY then DISCOUNT) and leaves the brand word tiny. Its characters are scattered at the edges and look like fragments. B reads left to right with DISCOUNT leading and MERRY plus a character cluster after it. That is more coherent and compact, but MERRY is still tiny, DISCOUNT comes before MERRY, and the characters are crammed together. B is slightly less bad.

A: reading order is jumbled (the 'Xavier Sport Program' line sits above 'by submitting to'). The text is left-ragged with mismatched alignments (centered headline, left-aligned lower lines). A stray blue bar is cropped at the top edge, the panel covers the racket, and the divider lines are stranded at the bottom. B: the panel is a clean, coherent block with the correct reading order (headline, then 'by submitting to Xavier Sport Program') and the ball and racket stay visible. Flaws: the text is crammed in the top half of the panel, leaving a large empty blue area below. 'by submitting to' and the program name are jammed on one line at different weights. The underline fragments hit 'submitting' and 'Program', and the empty thin outline box floats over the racket. The panel's stepped top edge also looks sloppy.

A: the magnifier icon is enlarged into a huge, pixelated focal point that competes with the headline. The search-box icon is lost, so the PPC bar has an empty box on the right. 'How to level up' is small, and the photo is jammed at the bottom with thin margins. Still, the order is correct (headline, PPC, ONLINE COURSE, photo), the orange brand is strong, and the text is readable. B: reading order is changed, with ONLINE COURSE above HOW TO LEVEL UP, so the message reads out of sequence. The photo is cropped into an odd oval-ish shape floating in a big empty white top area. The faint ghost magnifier at the bottom looks like an orphaned leftover. The text is small, and the PPC bar also has an empty box. The look is less orange-dominant and the original's feel is weakened. Both are flawed, but A keeps the hierarchy and brand better.

A: headline 'DEAN COOPER' is large and dominant. But the white panel is split, with a stray empty frame and two orphan dots on the right. 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' sits detached on the left, the pattern is cropped into a block, and the 'Opening' line is cramped against the panel edge. B: 'DEAN COOPER' is tiny and 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' is larger than the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. The reading order is jumbled, 'THE MINIMALIST' is microscopic and unreadable, and 'Opening' collides with the empty frame. Dots and frames are scattered, and the overall result is chaotic.

A keeps a left-to-right order: red 'New pasta menu' headline, then the photo panels, the plate illustration, and Cascadia/RESTAURANT/URL at the right. The photos are tiny, empty-looking tiles, and there is a dead blank frame. The headline is small, and the divider swooshes are stretched. B is more broken: the URL sits at the far left, apart from the brand. 'Cascadia' is jammed beside tiny thumbnails under the headline, and 'RESTAURANT' is stranded far from 'Cascadia'. The headline floats in the middle with no connection to its content, a large pasta-pattern block is dead space, and the photos are microscopic. B has no reading order and fragmented grouping.

Both are unusable. A has a readable headline at left, but the food photos are tiny thumbnails, a blank white frame sits empty, the pattern tile is a mess, and the brand name and URL are scattered along the bottom. B puts the photos in a tiny strip at the bottom-left, leaves the middle and right mostly empty, and shows a stray pattern block. Its headline is small and floating, and the brand, URL and 'RESTAURANT' are crammed together. A keeps clearer reading order and a stronger headline, so it is slightly less bad.

A is basically a scaled-down copy of the original centered on a narrow panel with empty grey bands on both sides. The quote and attribution stay legible and in order, and the brand is intact. But the text is small, the layout is not rearranged for the banner shape, and the side areas are dead space. B has a different layout, but it is broken. The quote and attribution sit in the top half of a large red block with a big empty red area below. A stray underline cuts through 'MODERN', and the stray rule lines are misplaced. The skyline is shrunk and cut off in a separate white panel with no connection to the text. The attribution floats to the right of the quote with a weak hierarchy.

A: the logo/icon and decorative shapes are squashed into a tiny strip at left-middle, cropped and nearly invisible, and the headline is off-centre in a 4-line stack with huge dead areas. B: a centred 3-line headline reads well and is dominant, but the wind-turbine icon is tiny and pushed to the bottom among cropped, distorted shapes, with a stray diagonal line, so the original's icon-above-title structure is lost.

Both are very wide, short banners. A: the headline is large and readable on the left, but the turbine icon is tiny and jammed into the right corner, overlapping the shapes. The green and blue triangles are crushed into a cluster, and there is a huge dead gap between the text and the graphics. B: the headline is smaller but centered, with the icon and shapes in a row beneath it. The result is cramped vertically, the text sits very close to the top edge, and the icon and triangles are tiny with faint decoration lines. B groups the elements more coherently and keeps the shapes distinct, so it is marginally less bad.

A scatters the SALE letters: a lone 'E' is top-left, 'SAL' is bottom-left, partly covered by a decoration, so the word is unreadable and out of order. The headline is offset, and a tiny decoration cluster sits mid-right with empty white-ish space around it. B keeps the headline large and readable on the left. Its S, A, L, E are in order but split around a lantern column, with stacked circles in the middle and decorations overlapping the letters. The 'L' is clipped against the 'E', and the lantern art is shrunk to tiny noise. B is still broken, but less so.

A keeps the SALE circles with the red tassel, which stays recognisable as the design, and the decorations fill the canvas. But the S, A and L letters are tiny and off-centre inside their circles, and only E is large. The circle column is jammed against the right edge. The headline is tiny and floats at the top. The two lantern groups are duplicated, and the layout is unbalanced. B drops the SALE circles entirely. The letters E, S, A, L sit as loose red text in the wrong order (E first), and they are detached from the headline. The headline is small and sits in the middle of dead space. The bottom is nearly empty, apart from a tiny fragment. Large areas are blank. The brand message is lost.

A keeps the full lockup (headline with the gold leaf wreath) centred on a calm dark area, so the brand survives. But the whole thing is tiny in a 768x71 banner, with lots of dead space and the food image cropped to a blur, so the headline is barely readable. B has the headline text slightly larger, but the gold wreath is split off and stranded on the right, drifting over the busy fig. The headline is left floating, without its decoration, off-centre and small. That breaks the brand lockup and looks like a bug.

A keeps the brand intact: a large two-line headline, a legible address diamond and date diamond, and a visible city photo. Flaws: the body copy is tiny, the empty diamond-outline pattern is a big dead area, the rule floats detached from the headline, the vertical URL is tiny, and the photo is a cropped small rectangle instead of the diamond collage. B is unusable: the city photo is shrunk to a ~30px thumbnail, the address diamond is isolated in the far right with illegible text, and the date diamond is tiny and jammed against the body copy. The URL is illegible, the rule is stranded, the layout is scattered and the headline has no visual support.

A: the logo shapes are shrunk and jammed against the left edge, and the headline touches the subhead with no gap. The body copy is tiny and the URL sits crammed beside it. Large dead areas remain top and bottom, and the hierarchy is weak. B: the logo is large and intact, and the headline is strong. The two-column split reads well for a banner, and the URL is legible. Flaws: the headline's last line nearly touches the right column, the subhead has ragged breaks ("YOU CANNOT" and "VIRTUAL" orphaned), and the legal text is tiny. The URL is also separated from its "follow the link" line. Margins are tight, but this is much more usable than A.

A scrambles the reading order: the product list sits above the price, 'for all drinkware on' is a tiny fragment far below the price, and the URL is a microscopic rotated string at the far left. The stripes are reduced to two stubs and a grey bar, so the brand's three-colour band is lost. B keeps the three stripes intact and the text in a logical order (price, tagline, URL, list). But the text is a tiny column in the middle of a huge empty banner, the URL stays rotated and unreadable, and the right two-thirds is dead space. B is the less bad of the two.

A: the 'Invites you to spend…' copy is crushed into a narrow column with one or two words per line, which is a terrible rag. The dates stack in a separate tiny column with awkward breaks, and the cross is blurry and oversized, wedged between text columns. The reading order is jumbled. The illustration is good and large. B: a clean centered text stack with a readable headline and subline, so the hierarchy and reading order survive. The flaws are a tiny mountain illustration pushed into the right corner and clipped near the edge, a lot of dead space, and small, blurry cross and dates/worship line that sit off the headline's axis. It is weak but legible and not broken.

A: the cross is blown up into a huge blurry, pixelated block that dominates the banner and competes with the headline. The headline is stacked in 5 short lines, the dates are ragged and left-aligned, and the illustration is squeezed at the bottom. The text is readable and the content order is intact. B: the layout is tidier at the top, with a compact headline and readable body. The dates break badly ("JULY / 2-18"). The illustration floats mid-canvas with a big dead gap above and below it. The tiny blurry cross is stranded at the bottom edge, cut off and detached from its "Worship & Bible Study" line. The composition reads as scattered, with an orphaned cross and uneven spacing. A is less bad because its content flows in order, but its cross is a major flaw.

A is a proper banner layout: large headline on the left, cat illustration on the right, readable, and the image is not distorted. Flaws: the art is small and sits tight against the right and bottom edges, and the top and bottom margins are uneven. B puts a tiny headline at the top centre with a small cat group below. The headline is much weaker than the original, there is dead space on both sides, and the cats are cropped at the bottom and cramped. It looks like a shrunk copy, not a banner layout.

A: hierarchy is inverted — 'food & drinks' is the giant headline and runs over the cup, while 'Order online' (the actual message/CTA) is tiny and stranded bottom-center; reading order is reversed and the rules float disconnected. B: keeps 'Order online' as bold headline above italic 'food & drinks', rules bracket the group like the original, and the type is large and legible. Flaws: 'Order online' overlaps the cup edge, 'drinks' butts against the box, the top rule is cramped, and the text block is crowded and slightly misaligned.

A: headline is small and sits mid-canvas over a busy shelf and white-box image. The blue info box floats at the top, detached from the headline and out of reading order (details before title). The black box is tiny with small text, the left alignments are inconsistent, and the large gaps between the three groups look arbitrary. B: the headline is larger and clearly dominant, with the blue box and black box stacked beneath it in a sensible order, and the text is more legible. Flaws: the headline sits on a busy image area, 'FURNITURE' in blue has weak contrast on the grey, a stray translucent grey bar sits at the top, and the layout is slightly left-heavy with uneven box widths.

A keeps the original's left-to-right order (headline, window, details) and uses the full width. The headline is large and bold, the details are readable, and margins are consistent. The window is a bit small and the headline sits close to the left edge. B shifts everything right and leaves a large dead area on the left. Its details text is tiny and almost illegible, and the small details block is detached from the headline. The headline is also small, so the hierarchy is weak and the composition is lopsided.

A keeps the headline dominant and centred, with owls at both ends and confetti between. But the eyebrow 'EVENT MANAGMENT' is tiny and stranded far left, the owls are small and cropped, and the headline sits close to the top edge. B has a tiny blue owl wedged under the eyebrow, with a pink star jammed against the text. The headline is small and crammed at the top, the upside-down owl is cropped at the right, and the composition is scattered with large dead areas, so the layout looks random.

A: reading order is scrambled (HOHOHO top, AGENCY at the bottom, tagline in the middle), the shapes are chopped into a fragmented strip, and 'Office Secret Santa' is small and wrapped awkwardly. B: AGENCY, tagline and HOHOHO stack in a clear text block and the shapes sit together at the edges. But the order is reversed (AGENCY above HOHOHO), the wavy lines run through the blue C, the shapes at the bottom are clustered and cut off, and the text is small.

A keeps the brick as the hero, but it is clipped at the right by the blue shape. The headline is broken as 'CONS TRUC TION' and is small. The text sits in a scattered row across the top and bottom, and the price is detached from 'Buy 2 only for' with the CTA between them. B drops the product: the brick is a tiny icon in the bottom-left corner and the large blue X is empty. The broken 'CONS TRUC TION' headline, price placed above the 'Buy 2' copy (wrong reading order), a CTA floating off to the right and big dead space make B worse.

A keeps the brick as a big hero and the yellow/blue brand, but the brick is cropped at the right edge and the pixelated image is stretched. The headline is small and broken into 'CONS TRUC TION', the price is separated from 'Buy 2 only for', and the CTA is small and sits between them in a weak footer row. B shrinks the brick to a tiny, cut-off icon at the bottom, leaving the large blue X shape empty and dominant. Its headline is tiny and also broken, and the price sits away from its copy. The layout is scattered with dead space and no focal point, so it is worse than A.

Both lose the hands photo, which is the original's key imagery, leaving only a small black rectangle and a mostly white banner. A keeps the quote and attribution as separate, readable elements with clear spacing. However, the attribution floats far right and the photo is gone. B crams the attribution tight under the quote with almost no gap, leaves stray ghost white cloud/plus fragments at the left, and the image sliver is a tiny cropped black box, so it looks more broken.

Both are unusable: the hands photo, the heart of the original, is missing in each. A has the quote and attribution split far apart. The attribution floats alone on the right, a stray black bar pokes in at the top edge, and there is a stray tiny mark at the far right. B keeps the quote and attribution together as one centered block, with the attribution slightly larger and clearer. But B's text is tiny, there is a white cloud/plus fragment on the left that reads as a leftover artifact, and a black bar sits at the bottom edge. B is less bad because of its grouping and reading order.

Both lose the hero photo of praying hands: A crops it to a black strip at the top, leaving a ghosted white cross fragment at left and a big empty bottom. B is worse: it slices the photo into two black rectangles, one at the top and one at the bottom, with white crosses on black that look like stray artifacts, plus the cloud shapes become faint white outlines at left. B's quote and name are also cramped together. A's text is clean and readable with a clear hierarchy, so it is the less bad of the two.

A keeps the design recognisable: the yellow headline box, the photo and the thin frame survive. But it is a tiny narrow strip in the middle of a wide white canvas, so the headline is very small, the photo is cropped and the sides are dead empty. A stray yellow block is clipped at the top. B is broken: the photo and headline are thumbnail-sized and stranded in the lower left, the canvas is mostly blank, and there are orphaned tick marks and an empty outlined box on the right plus a stray yellow sliver. It does not read as the same design.

A keeps the 'LOVE. CARE. KIDS.' headline in a yellow box with a thin frame and a reasonably sized photo, so the message and image survive. But the elements are scattered: a stray yellow bar at the top, floating tick marks beside the photo, and a big empty frame with the photo off to the right. The headline box sits outside the photo, so the hierarchy is weak. B is unusable. The photo is a tiny thumbnail in the bottom-left corner and the headline is a small box at the top-left. Four tick marks float alone, there is a large empty outlined rectangle, and a stray bar sits at the top. It loses the hero image and has no composition.

A is scattered: URL far left, headline crammed in the middle with tiny blank swatches, photos shrunk to thumbnails, 'RESTAURANT' separated from 'Cascadia', and a stray pattern tile and divider. Nothing reads as a group and the hero photos are lost. B has a left-to-right order (headline, divider, photos, frame, plate, brand and URL block) with the brand text grouped and legible. But the photos are tiny, there are empty beige and white panels, and the headline is cramped at the left edge. Both are unusable, B less so.

A is broken: the headline is crammed into the top-left of a mostly empty red block with a stray line crossing 'MODERN', the author sits as a disconnected fragment on the right, and the skyline is shrunk and floats in a white panel, so the design is no longer recognisable. B keeps the original composition (white frame, red panel, centred headline, author, skyline) letterboxed on a grey field. The text is small but readable. The skyline crowds the author line and the red panel bottom, and the wide grey margins are wasted, but it is clearly the same design.

A: the headline is large and readable and centred. But the wind-turbine logo is tiny, jammed into a strip of squashed, clipped shapes along the bottom, and the large empty middle holds only one stray line. B: the logo is a tiny icon in a cramped strip of cropped shapes at the left, offset from the headline. The text block is off-centre to the right, leaving random stray lines and large dead areas. The composition has no clear intent.

Both are ~320x50 banners, so tiny that everything is hard to read. A: the headline is minuscule, with text far too small to read, and the wind-turbine icon is replaced by a few small indistinct shapes (green, blue, red) and faint lines. The brand mark is lost. B: the headline is much larger and readable, and a turbine icon survives next to the triangles. The decor is cramped at the far right and the icon is very small. The layout is left-heavy with a large empty gap in the middle, but it is still clearly the better of the two.

A keeps a compact text block (AGENCY, Office Secret Santa, HOHOHO) in a right column with decorations clustered together. The reading order is wrong, with HOHOHO below the subtitle. The wavy red lines overlap the big blue C, the triangles and dots at the bottom are jumbled, and the shapes are tiny and crowded. B scatters the text across the canvas: HOHOHO sits at the top, the subtitle is squeezed into a small two-line block mid-right, and AGENCY is at the bottom, so the lockup is broken. B's decorative shapes are fragmented and clipped, and the layout looks random. B also has large dead areas. A is the less bad.

A keeps the quote and attribution together as one centred block. But the photo of the hands is gone, the cloud shapes are faint white-on-white fragments on the left, a black bar is cut off at the bottom edge, and the text is tiny. B splits the quote and 'MAHATMA GANDHI' far apart across the banner, so they read as unrelated. B also has a black block clipped at the top edge, a stray faint mark at the far right, no image, and a large dead area in the middle.

Both lose the hands photo, the key image, and are broken. A: text is readable and well grouped, and the lower black strip with white crosses at least keeps the brand motif. But the image is cut into two meaningless black bands, the cloud shape is a ghost on the left, and the layout is off-balance with dead white space. B: only a black strip at the top is left, with no recognisable image at all. The crosses are faint, white-on-white and fragmented. The CTA/author gap is loose, and the bottom third is empty, so it is a bare text slide that has lost the original design.

A is essentially unusable: the photo and headline are shrunk to a tiny thumbnail in the lower left, with stray dashes, an empty outline box and a yellow sliver scattered over a mostly blank 768x200 canvas. B keeps the photo and yellow headline panel as one recognisable unit with a readable 'LOVE. CARE. KIDS.', but it is a narrow portrait strip in the middle of a wide banner with large dead white areas on both sides. The yellow block is cut off at the top and overlaps the frame, the photo is cropped, and nothing uses the banner width.

Both are unusable: a very wide banner where the hero barrel photo is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail and the paper-tear texture floats as an empty pale rectangle. A has the thumbnail and logo jammed beside a tiny dash under the title, and the tagline pushed to the right edge, so it is nearly cut off. B has a stray dark smeared bar under the title, which looks like a rendering glitch, and a tiny photo and logo under the tagline. B's tagline is better placed with margin, and its title and tagline read more cleanly. A's cramped edge-hugging tagline and its misaligned photo, dash and logo cluster are slightly worse. B's dark bar is a clear flaw, so the edge is slim.

A just shrinks the square design into a centred column inside a wide canvas. The yellow band stops short of the edges, leaving big dead blue side bars, and the whole layout looks letterboxed. Text is tiny: the list is small and the yellow CTA is fine print. The doctor is cropped at the bottom and the list sits cramped beside the hand. B reflows for the banner. The headline is large and the hashtag is a badge beside it. The list is on the left, the doctor is in the centre and the CTA is on the right, so it reads left to right with readable text. Flaws: the hashtag badge is tiny and stuck to the headline, the 'breath Dry cough' wrap is inherited from the original, the doctor is smaller and cropped at the bottom, and the CTA is a bit loose from the figure.

A is broken: the white panel and frame are scattered, an empty white rectangle with a stray dot sits on the right, and the dots are detached from the name. The 'The Minimalist' band is cut off at the left edge, the opening line is tiny, and the text panel overlaps the art. B keeps the original composition as a scaled-down centered card with a frame, dots and band intact. Its flaws: the artwork fills only the middle ~70% of the canvas, leaving empty white side margins. The text is small, and 'Opening' is fine print.

A: the pattern background is gone, leaving a white canvas with a stray empty white frame at right and tiny dots at the far edges. The headline is tiny and crammed at the top, the subtitle and date are microscopic and jammed together, and the title is cut off at the top. B: it keeps a slice of the pattern behind a larger DEAN COOPER, with a readable DDG STUDIO PRESENTS at left, so the headline stays dominant. It still has a stray empty white box with two dots at right, a tiny date line, and a mostly white canvas that loses the original's colour and brand feel.

A keeps the label frame and the bottle illustrations along the bottom, so it still reads as the same design. But the headline rules are misplaced: one runs through the gap between J'adore Paris and LAVANDER and sits off to the right, another stray rule floats at the lower right, and the text is small and crooked. B separates the label panel from its text: the panel is an empty white box with a stray dash, and the text sits on the bare background with the brand name pushed to the right edge. The illustrations are shrunk to a tiny strip and a blurry oversized butterfly and cookie fragment appear. B is unusable.

Both are tiny 320x50-style banners with the design reduced to illegible fragments. A has a clear left-to-right order: 'New pasta menu' headline in red, a large Cascadia wordmark, the URL and a RESTAURANT label. Its flaws are that the food photos are reduced to tiny thumbnails, the orange swashes are stray fragments, and the headline is cramped at three lines in a thin strip. B scrambles the order, with the URL first and a faint doodle, then a headline that is crammed and appears to run into the Cascadia wordmark. B also has an orange block, unreadable thumbnails and a loose RESTAURANT label at the far right, so it looks jumbled and its hierarchy is weaker.

A uses the wide banner shape well. The red panel runs left to right with the headline and attribution, and the skyline sits at the right. Flaws: the headline is small, the author line is tiny, the headline and author are not aligned, and the skyline is cropped and walled off from the panel. B is a tiny centered copy of the original in a huge empty grey canvas. The text is illegible, the skyline is mangled and overlaps the panel, and the layout does not fit the format at all.

A reads left to right, with both owls visible and the headline large. But 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' is stranded far left, away from the headline, and the order is reversed (eyebrow, then confetti, then owls, then title). The owls are small and touch the headline. The confetti is a tiny dead patch, and the left side is mostly empty. B puts the headline above the eyebrow, which is a wrong reading order. Its owls are microscopic and clipped against the bottom edge, the text is small, the right third is only tiny confetti, and the characters that carry the brand are lost.

A: the eyebrow "EVENT MANAGEMENT" is pinned at the top, far from the headline, so the title-to-subtitle order breaks. Confetti is stranded in the upper area with a big dead gap, and the headline sits low and nearly touches the right edge. The owls are tiny and hold no weight, though the owls-plus-headline lockup is reasonably intentional. B: the headline and subtitle are grouped and in correct reading order, with a clean left margin and good size. The owls are minuscule and jammed into the bottom-left corner, and the confetti floats in the middle with large empty gaps, so the mascots lose their prominence and the composition is unbalanced.

A: text is large and centered with decent hierarchy, but the logo is tiny and crammed into a top strip with shapes clipped at the edge, the headline is jammed to the bottom, and the lines are stray fragments. B: the text is pushed off-axis to the right, the red triangle is stranded mid-left, and the logo is a tiny icon at the bottom edge, cramped among clipped shapes. Hierarchy is weaker and the layout looks more random than A, where the logo at least leads the reading order.

A: headline 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' is large and readable, but the SALE word is broken: S alone at left, empty circles in the middle, A L E scattered at right, with clutter from the lantern art, so the focal element is lost. B: keeps the original symmetric structure with the vertical SALE stack, but it is shrunk onto a very wide, short strip, so the headline is only a few pixels tall and the SALE letters and decorations are barely visible. Nothing is legible. It is a shrunk copy, not a rearranged design.

A: DISCOUNT sits above 'MERRY' so the order reads backwards; the headline is reduced to a tiny strip and the monsters are a thin row jammed at the bottom edge, with a dead area above. B: 'MERRY' is tiny, shrunk to a fraction of DISCOUNT and unreadable, buried in the character row. DISCOUNT is crammed against the right edge. The character row is cramped, and the tree and Merry text are nearly illegible. Both are poor; A keeps MERRY a bit more legible and has a tidier band, though its order is wrong.

A keeps all three color bars together as the brand signature on the left, and the price is big and clear. But "for all drinkware on" is a tiny 3-line fragment stranded far from the price, the URL is a tiny rotated string floating in the middle, and the list is small and ragged at the right edge. B breaks the bars: grey is full height, blue and red shrink to tiny stubs, so the palette is lost. Its "for all drinkware on" is tiny and floats above the price, the list is tiny, and the vertical URL is jammed at the left edge. B's price is bigger, but it is unbalanced with dead space.

A: "food & drinks" is split from "Order online" and sits on top of the box, so the "drinks" text collides with the carton. The headline shrinks to tiny text and ends up bigger-looking subordinate to the tagline. The two rules are far apart and frame nothing, and the message is fragmented. B: the lockup is kept together as in the original, with rules above and below, a bold headline and an italic subline, and it doesn't touch the image. Flaws: the text block is small for the wide banner and has a lot of dead space on the left, the cluster floats slightly right of centre in the empty area, and the tagline is small.

A: 'food & drinks' is set huge and runs over the cardboard boxes, so 'drinks' sits on a busy image. It also outweighs the 'Order online' headline, so the hierarchy is inverted, and the two lines are split with a large gap. B: 'food & drinks' is smaller and clears the boxes, so it reads cleanly. 'Order online' is still the bold headline, but it is crammed against the left edge with a stray rule line running through 'online' (it looks like an underline or overlap). The row is also unevenly spaced with dead space on the right, and there is no CTA.

A fills the wide short canvas well: headline is large and bold, window large, and the details are legible and right-aligned in a clear left-to-right order. Flaws: the headline's 'Sunday' almost touches the window, the details block is jammed against the right edge, margins are tight and uneven, and the window is nearly clipped at top and bottom. B shrinks everything. Headline and details are tiny, and the details text is very small and thin. It leaves large dead space on all sides, with the cluster floating in the middle and a weak hierarchy. This is a shrunk copy of the original rather than a rearrangement.

A keeps the original's order of headline, window, then details, so it still reads as the same design. Its flaws are a tight left margin on the headline, a stained-glass window that looks cropped and jammed against the top and bottom edges, and a three-line details block set very small and right-aligned. B moves the window to the far left, which breaks the original reading order.
